summary: Boris Turayev worked in history and archaeology after studying at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (c. 1886–1891). He held posts at Imperial St. Petersburg University (c. 1896–1918) and Saint Petersburg State University (c. 1918–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy around 1920 to 1928. From around 1928 to 1937, he served at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Boris Vladimirtsov worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at St. Petersburg University and under Antoine Meillet, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (c. 1915–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Shri Singha Shedra and under traditional teachers Tubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam.

Brad Warner is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Kent State University and under Tim McCarthy, Gudō Wafu Nishijima, and Gyomay Kubose. He became head of Dogen Sangha International in 2007 and founded Dogen Sangha Los Angeles in 2012.

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, Harvard University (M.T.S., 1993), and the University of Virginia (B.A. 1989; Ph.D. 2004), where he was supervised by David Germano.
Bradley L. Herling is a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held an attested post at Marymount Manhattan College in 2008.

Braj Basi Lal was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at SOAS (c. 2005–2010) and the University of Munich (c. 2010–2019).
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Louisville under advisor Patrick Arthur Pranke, attested in 2015.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta and completed his doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was the Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (c. 1980–1985) and became an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

Bret W. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto universities. He taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin universities and held philosophy professorships at Loyola University Maryland attested in 2007 and 2018.
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the instruction of Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from around 1963 to 1967 and was a student of Ngawang Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (c. 1999–2018) before becoming a Japanese Studies professor and chair at Bates College around 2018.

Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history who completed degrees at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities. He held academic positions at the University of Auckland, Antioch University (2005–2013), and the University of Adelaide (c. 2003–2015).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under the doctoral supervision of György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Haileybury and Fort William colleges, he served in Nepal as Assistant Resident starting in 1820 and as British Resident from around 1833 to 1843.

Brian J. Nichols is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his PhD at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Anne C. Klein, attested in 2011.
